doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What family abroad say about America: George Floyd and leadership
summary: Parents and Europeans talk about America, fearing unrest after George Floyd's killing; she wants leadership and sees some good examples.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: What do your parents in Australia — do they make observations?

Oh yes. The whole world does, don’t they, about America. They love to talk about America. The whole world. All the time. Europeans, they call me, they talk about America. My family. My aunts, my uncles, my cousins, everybody wants to talk about America right now. We are in the world focus right now.
Can you share what you are hearing?

Dissatisfaction with the president. They like to talk about that. Fear about the next coming months, what it might bring and pain and anguish over the brutality of the George Floyd situation, the murder of this man, you know, and the consequences of that, and the protests. A lot of fear. I think the whole world is looking at America with what’s next. And just hoping that we come out of this with some positivity and some leadership. We need leadership. That’s what I feel. That’s what’s really lacking you know. There are

segments of it, you know, I feel like sometimes Andrew Cuomo in New York has done a good job at certain things. You know there are bits of good leadership, there are good cops shining through. There are people trying to lead the way and show positivity. We just need so much more of it.
Well it’s a hard subject to talk about because it’s so sad you know.
